# ICM Master

> A poker tournament trainer built around ICM, the Independent Chip Model, which
> converts a chip stack into the share of the prize pool it is worth. Nine-player
> tables, ranges, hand analysis, coaching and realistic tournament decisions.

## WebMCP tools

The landing page at `https://mehrdadabedin.github.io/poker-icm-coach/` declares WebMCP tools
with `document.modelContext.registerTool`. An agent should call these tools instead of scraping
the HTML. They answer from the same data the page renders, in a closed shape. Registration is
guarded, so the tools exist only in a browser that supports WebMCP.

### describe
What this page is and what else can be asked.
Input: none.
Returns: `{ page, purpose, sections: string[], tools: string[] }`

### list_features
The app's capabilities, read from the features section.
Input: none.
Returns: `{ features: [{ name, summary }] }`

### explain_icm_term
Defines one tournament concept, why it matters and an example.
Input: `{ term }`, one of `icm`, `bubble`, `risk_premium`, `push_fold`, `spr`.
Returns: `{ term, definition, why_it_matters, example }`

### get_quickstart
How to run the project locally.
Input: none.
Returns: `{ requirements: string[], steps: [{ label, command }], note }`

## Project facts

- 9-player Texas Hold'em tournament trainer: 1 human hero, 8 AI opponents with distinct personalities (tight, aggressive, TAG, loose, LAG, passive, balanced, adaptive).
- Exact Independent Chip Model equity for up to 9 players, plus tournament-stage detection, bubble pressure, risk premium, push/fold engine, 13x13 range matrix, SPR and board texture.
- Coach engine has three detail levels, BEGINNER, INTERMEDIATE and ADVANCED; the app
  ships ADVANCED. Test mode grades a decision PREFERRED, ACCEPTABLE or SUBOPTIMAL after you act.
- Session review covers hand history, VPIP, PFR, aggression, coach agreement, ICM mistakes, position and stack performance, biggest-leak detection.
- Tournament defaults: 45,000 starting chips, 100/100 blinds, 20-minute levels, blind timer with a fast mode. Antes: none, traditional or big-blind ante.
- Stack: React + TypeScript + Vite front end. Python 3.12 + FastAPI + Pydantic v2 + SQLAlchemy 2 back end. PostgreSQL via Alembic. Android packaging via Capacitor.
- The backend owns all game state and the frontend renders snapshots. The AI never sees hidden cards or future streets.
